TWO VERIFIED LIMITATIONS. (1) Grid resolution: 52 of 77 districts share a byte-identical daily rainfall series with at least one neighboring district (NASA POWER's spatial resolution is coarser than the distance between some district centroids); there are only 45 independent climate signals across 77 districts, not 77. See climate_grid_clusters.csv for the full grouping -- do not compare rainfall between two districts in the same cluster. (2) Structural break: national mean rainfall roughly doubles between the 1990-2003 and 2004-2019 periods in a single-year jump, consistent with a known transition in NASA's precipitation data sourcing (reanalysis-only before ~2000-2004, blended with satellite-based GPM/TRMM retrievals after). Restrict trend and baseline-vs-recent anomaly calculations to 2004-2026; the full 1990-2026 record remains valid for extreme-day/percentile threshold characterization only.
